design_status: informed amendment after the initial C++/Python subtraction study; not an untouched preregistration

amendment.reason: The first study exposed cancellation in the existing subtractive Python call-spread baseline. A binary64 Python/SciPy digital-strike integral was therefore added to compare against the stable mathematical representation in the same ordinary precision.
amendment.changes: add six Python binary64 quadrature quantities and their high-precision errors; retain original contracts, meshes, thresholds and subtraction comparison; add two disclosed implementation stress contracts covering the otherwise unexecuted positive-integral C++ branch and an extremely broad strike interval
amendment.retained_record: amendment_history.json contains the initial protocol, its hash and the observed outcomes motivating each amendment
amendment.binary64_implementation_development: The first stronger-baseline run retained a small-volatility Gamma cancellation failure. A subsequently inspected actual-fallback contract exposed precision loss in log(S/K); the standard log1p((S-K)/K) expression for nearby spot and strike was therefore used. Earlier results remain retained. No tolerance was relaxed.
amendment.broad_interval_addition: A numerical review then found loss of the upper-strike normal coordinate for K=1e-300, cap=spot=100, volatility=1e-8, rate=yield=0. The native endpoint evaluation was corrected and this additional informed stress case retained without changing any earlier tolerance. The direct binary64 integral is evaluated as written, with any resulting cancellation failures retained.
amendment.prior_record_status: self-contained machine-readable history supplied with this study; initial outcomes informed this amendment
amendment.threshold_status: original 2e-11 scaled absolute plus 2e-11 relative analytic tolerance unchanged for both C++ and stronger Python baseline

data_status: entirely synthetic; no market observations or licensed data
model: risk-neutral GBM with continuous dividend yield; capped European call

greek_units.theta: per year of calendar time; minus maturity derivative

comparison_roles.cpp_python_analytic: cross-language consistency; shared formula is not an independent financial baseline
comparison_roles.python_binary64_integral: ordinary binary64 SciPy quadrature of the same derived digital-strike representation; stronger stable Python baseline, not independent empirical evidence
comparison_roles.cpp_python_pde: matched backward-Euler discretisation; distinct Thomas/DST implementations
comparison_roles.analytic_reference: closed-form dominant baseline for this specified model
comparison_roles.mp_integral: 80-digit integral of digital calls over strikes, differentiated under the integral; separate numerical representation under the same GBM
comparison_roles.mp_call_spread: 100-digit call-spread check on the quadrature reference

pde_scope: fixed nine-sigma domain, ordinary kinked payoff, identical finite bumps; numerical refinement is not a convergence proof or a complete error certificate
relative_error_rule: report only when abs(reference)>1e-12*quantity_scale; otherwise null
quantity_scale_rule: positive dimensional scales derived from discounted cap, spot, maturity and volatility, including the narrow-spread scale
fallback_branch_check_scope: additional informed price-only relative check for the new positive_integral_fallback contract; standard near-zero threshold would otherwise make the price check uninformative; no threshold changes to the original eighteen contracts
failure_roles: Native/reference/PDE failures determine implementation status. Stronger Python integral failures remain explicit baseline diagnostics. The comparison does not claim that every method passed when baseline diagnostics fail.
limitations: High-precision arithmetic and quadrature are numerical references, not outward-rounded certificates.
No empirical model validation or quantum advantage follows from these comparisons.
All failure rows are retained; a stress failure cannot be removed from the aggregate status.
Fixed-domain, finite-bump errors are separated from analytic bump bias.
These timing-free comparisons do not identify a language speedup.
The stronger Python baseline was added after observing the original subtraction failures; it is an informed amendment.
QUADPACK estimates are diagnostic error estimates and omit a proof of binary64 rounding error; they are not certificates.
